lessons.titleZh: 與另一件事緊密交纏

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Her worries were wrapped up with the coming exam.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page133, table1, row4; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Closely entangled or connected with another concern or experience.
brief.meaningZh: 與另一項顧慮或經驗緊密交纏。
brief.grammar: one feeling is wrapped up with another concern; identify the two connected things. Distinguish this contextual connection metaphor from finishing a meeting or a person being absorbed in work.
brief.register: Contextual figurative connection, not a claim that every wrap-up-with construction has one fixed meaning.
brief.boundaryZh: 連繫不表示兩事相同，也未說所有感受只由一個原因造成。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需看主語：感受與另一顧慮交纏，不是聚會已結束，也不是紙包物件。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明兩項感受或顧慮的關係，並澄清自己真正介意甚麼。

listening.en: My excitement about the first exhibition was wrapped up with worry about showing my drawings to my old teacher; I wanted her to see them, but her opinion mattered more to me than the visitor numbers.
listening.zh: 首次展覽的興奮與向舊老師展示畫作的擔心交纏；我想讓她看，但比起訪客數，我更在意她的意見。
listening.promptZh: 說話者的感受怎樣連在一起？

options.en: The exhibition was exciting, while the old teacher’s opinion also made it personally worrying.
options.zh: 展覽令人興奮，而舊老師的意見也令說話者特別擔心。

options.en: The worry concerned visitor numbers, rather than the teacher’s response.
options.zh: 擔心的是訪客人數，不是老師的反應。

options.en: The teacher had already reviewed every drawing before the speaker felt excited.
options.zh: 說話者興奮前，老師已評過每張畫。

options.en: The exhibition had finished, and the speaker was packing the drawings away.
options.zh: 展覽已結束，說話者正在收起畫作。

listening.explanationZh: 興奮與在意老師意見同時存在；wrapped up with在此連起感受及顧慮，不是收展。

reply.promptEn: Why did the exhibition feel exciting and worrying at the same time?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼展覽同時令人興奮又擔心？

options.en: My excitement was wrapped up with how much my old teacher’s opinion mattered to me.
options.zh: 我的興奮與自己多在意舊老師的意見交纏。

options.en: I wanted to share the drawings, but I cared deeply about one visitor’s response.
options.zh: 我想分享畫作，但很在意其中一位訪客的反應。

options.en: Showing the work also meant letting someone important to me judge it.
options.zh: 展示作品也表示讓一個對我重要的人評它。

options.en: The teacher’s visit made the public event feel personally significant.
options.zh: 老師到訪令這公開活動對我有個人意義。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都連起展示的期待與老師回應的重要性，沒有把主要顧慮改成人數。

scene.promptZh: 朋友很期待第一次獨居，也掛念每天與妹妹吃早餐；她不是後悔搬家，只是兩種感受分不開。哪句貼切？

options.en: Her excitement about moving was wrapped up with sadness about leaving their shared mornings.
options.zh: 她對搬家的興奮，與離開共同早晨的難過交纏。

options.en: She felt sad only because the new flat had already been rented to somebody else.
options.zh: 她難過只是因新居已租給別人。

options.en: She had decided to cancel the move and keep every part of her old routine.
options.zh: 她已決定取消搬家，保留所有舊作息。

scene.explanationZh: 期待新生活與失去共同早晨可同時存在，不等於取消搬家。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種情況最不像本課 wrapped up with 所說的交纏關係？

options.en: 一項期待與在意某人的反應連在一起。
兩個問題在這個人的經驗中互相牽連。
主持人結束會議，請大家離場。

contrast.explanationZh: 結束會議可用wrap up，但不是此處感受或問題緊密相連的意思。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「你擔心老師看畫，是不是根本不想辦展？」你其實想分享，只很在意她的看法。哪句回答最好？

options.en: I do want the exhibition; the excitement is wrapped up with caring about her response.
options.zh: 我確實想辦展；興奮與在意她的回應交纏。

options.en: I should postpone the whole exhibition until I feel no worry about her response.
options.zh: 我應等到完全不擔心她的反應，才辦整個展覽。

options.en: I think getting a bigger audience would settle my concern about what she thinks.
options.zh: 我想多找觀眾，就可處理自己對她看法的顧慮。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先澄清想分享與在意老師並存；等完全不擔心或只增觀眾，沒有回應這兩種感受的關係。

speaking.en: My excitement was wrapped up with worry about how someone important to me would respond.
speaking.zh: 我的興奮與擔心一個重要的人會怎樣回應交纏。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說清哪兩項感受或顧慮連在一起。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你不想再做社團文案，但怕離任會把工作留給好友；這顧慮令你難分自己想做的角色。你想先一起列可交接工作，再談留下或轉角色，不因內疚便答應再做全年。用一至兩句英文協商。

examples.en: My reluctance to leave is wrapped up with concern about the work you would inherit. Could we list what could be handed over before deciding whether I should stay in this role for another year?
examples.zh: 我對離任的猶豫，與擔心你會接手的工作交纏；可先列可交接的部分，再決定我是否應再留這角色一年嗎？

examples.en: My choice of role is wrapped up with worry about leaving you a larger workload, so I want to separate the two questions. Let us discuss a handover as well as what I actually want to contribute.
examples.zh: 我的角色選擇與怕留較多工作給你交纏，所以想分兩問題；一起談交接，也談我真正想貢獻甚麼吧。

writing.selfCheckZh: 將角色意願與好友負擔分開討論，提出交接資訊再決定，不只保證留下或重述不捨。

takeaways.en: Her pride in the finished quilt was wrapped up with memories of the aunt who had taught her to sew.
takeaways.zh: 她對完成被子的自豪，與教她縫紉的姨媽的回憶交纏。

takeaways.en: His wish to keep the shop was wrapped up with concern for the neighbours who met there each morning.
takeaways.zh: 他想保留店舖的願望，與對每天在那相聚的鄰居的關心交纏。

review.author: AI root

english.evidence: Source preserves with connection reading. Collins wrapped-up-in entry supports related involvement/bound-up sense but does not separately attest this exact with-frame: https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/wrapped-up-in . Teach supplied image contextually, do not mislabel it as finish-a-meeting or absorb-person frame.

lessons.titleZh: 留住當下的一刻

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: She took one photo to capture the moment.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page133, table1, row5; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Preserve the character of a particular experience through an image, words or memory.
brief.meaningZh: 透過影像、文字或記憶，留住某個經驗當刻的特色。
brief.grammar: capture/captured the moment in a photograph/sketch/description; the article points to a particular moment, not every detail of an event.
brief.register: Natural figurative collocation about representation and memory.
brief.boundaryZh: 留住一刻不等於完整記錄整件事，亦不表示擺拍與自然發生的事件相同。
brief.misconceptionZh: 作品能保留某種感覺，也必然有選擇角度及範圍。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明自己想保留的細節，分清原來一刻與之後的重演。

listening.en: I made a quick sketch to capture the moment when Grandpa recognised his old schoolfriend at the gate; I kept their surprised smiles, rather than trying to draw everyone at the reunion.
listening.zh: 爺爺在門口認出舊同學時，我速寫留住那一刻；我畫下他們驚喜的笑容，沒打算畫聚會所有人。
listening.promptZh: 這幅速寫想保留甚麼？

options.en: The surprise of two friends recognising each other, rather than a complete record of the reunion.
options.zh: 兩位朋友認出彼此的驚喜，不是聚會完整紀錄。

options.en: The planned pose that everyone held for the official group picture.
options.zh: 所有人為正式合照擺好的姿勢。

options.en: The gate’s measurements so that the school could rebuild it.
options.zh: 門口尺寸，好讓學校重建。

options.en: Every person and conversation across the whole reunion.
options.zh: 整場聚會的每個人及每段談話。

listening.explanationZh: 認出同學及驚喜笑容界定所留一刻；速寫不是全場清單。

reply.promptEn: Why did you sketch those two smiles?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你畫下那兩個笑容？

options.en: I wanted to capture the moment when they recognised each other.
options.zh: 我想留住他們認出彼此的一刻。

options.en: Their surprise was the part of the reunion I especially wanted to remember.
options.zh: 他們的驚喜是我特別想記住的聚會片段。

options.en: The expression on their faces mattered more to this sketch than including everybody.
options.zh: 對這速寫而言，面上的表情比包括所有人重要。

options.en: I was keeping a brief encounter rather than documenting the whole event.
options.zh: 我在保留一段短暫相遇，不是記錄整個活動。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代選擇該片刻的目的，沒有把速寫說成全場紀錄。

scene.promptZh: 你錯過朋友收到好消息的即時反應，之後請她重演笑容拍照；你想準確分清照片與原來一刻。哪句最好？

options.en: The later photograph recreates her reaction; it does not capture the moment when she first heard the news.
options.zh: 後來照片重演她的反應，沒有記下首次聽消息的一刻。

options.en: The later pose records the very first reaction exactly as it happened.
options.zh: 後來的擺拍記錄了當時真正的首次反應。

options.en: The later pose can be used as direct evidence of her spontaneous expression before the camera was ready.
options.zh: 後來擺拍可直接證明相機準備好前，她自然流露的表情。

scene.explanationZh: 重演仍可有紀念價值，但時間及性質與原來反應不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種主張最不能只由 capture the moment 得出？

options.en: 影像或文字想保留某一刻的感覺。
作品必定完整而不經選擇地記下整個活動。
作者可說明自己選擇了哪個細節。

contrast.explanationZh: 保留一刻是有範圍的呈現，不等於全活動完整紀錄。

dialogue.promptZh: 爺爺問：「你沒畫其他人，是不是速寫還未完成？」你本來就只想留住重遇的笑容。哪句回應最好？

options.en: It is complete for what I wanted: I was trying to capture the moment you recognised your friend.
options.zh: 就我的目的已完成；我想留住你認出朋友的一刻。

options.en: I could add more faces so it becomes a record of who attended the reunion.
options.zh: 我可加更多面孔，讓它成為出席聚會的人物紀錄。

options.en: I would judge whether it is finished mainly by how much background colour I have added.
options.zh: 我會主要按加了多少背景顏色，判它是否完成。

dialogue.explanationZh: 問題是速寫是否完成其保留重逢表情的目的，不是改作出席紀錄或以背景量判完成。

speaking.en: I wanted to capture the moment in a few lines, especially the surprise on their faces.
speaking.zh: 我想用幾筆留住那一刻，尤其面上的驚喜。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說明想保留哪一刻及哪個細節。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替照片寫「她因首次獨奏而害怕」，本人卻說當時轉頭是在聽幕後小提琴，不是怕。你想更正圖說，保留照片捕捉到的轉頭一刻，另問能否引用她的解釋，不用影像直接替她定感受。用一至兩句英文回覆。

examples.en: The photograph captures the moment you turned towards the stage, but it does not establish why. I will correct the caption; may I quote your explanation that you were listening to the violin?
examples.zh: 照片留住你轉向舞台的一刻，卻未確立原因；我會改圖說，可引你說當時在聽小提琴的解釋嗎？

examples.en: I wanted to capture the moment, but I added a feeling you did not describe. I am sorry; could the new caption name the visible turn and, with your agreement, explain what you were listening to?
examples.zh: 我想留住一刻，卻加了你沒說的感受；對不起，新圖說可寫看得到的轉頭，再經你同意說在聽甚麼嗎？

writing.selfCheckZh: 承認影像可留動作而未證感受，更正自己的推測，先問本人能否引用解釋。

takeaways.en: Her two-line diary entry captured the moment the empty room filled with applause.
takeaways.zh: 她兩行日記留住空房間響起掌聲的一刻。

takeaways.en: The blurred photograph still captured the moment our dog noticed us at the station.
takeaways.zh: 模糊照片仍留住愛犬在車站發現我們的一刻。

english.evidence: Teach natural representation collocation, not a requirement for exhaustive documentary evidence; source taxonomy refined from fixed idiom to productive capture+moment wording.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese personally compared against each English subject, polarity, qualification and referent; no human approval claimed.

lessons.titleZh: 從某事得到樂趣或刺激

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Some visitors get their kicks from fast rides.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page133, table1, row6; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Get enjoyment or excitement from a particular activity.
brief.meaningZh: 從某項活動獲得樂趣或刺激。
brief.grammar: get one’s kicks from + noun/-ing; possessive agrees with the experiencer; get/got/getting.
brief.register: Informal expression, often playful and occasionally disapproving according to the activity and tone.
brief.boundaryZh: 不一定關乎危險、踢人或傷害；說話者喜歡的事也未必人人喜歡。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要看from後的活動，以及是善意自述還是批評以別人不快取樂。
brief.outcomeZh: 能自然描述自己喜歡怎樣尋樂，回應不同偏好而不替人下判斷。

listening.en: My cousins get their kicks from solving the trickiest clues at our weekly puzzle night; I prefer drawing the little maps, so we enjoy the same evening in different ways.
listening.zh: 表親每周解謎夜從最難線索得到樂趣；我較喜歡畫小地圖，所以同一晚各有不同樂趣。
listening.promptZh: 這裏 kicks 指甚麼？

options.en: The cousins’ enjoyment of working out difficult clues.
options.zh: 表親解開難線索的樂趣。

options.en: The cousins’ wish to stop the weekly gathering.
options.zh: 表親想停止每周聚會的願望。

options.en: The speaker’s preference for the same clue-solving task.
options.zh: 說話者同樣偏好解線索任務。

options.en: A payment the cousins receive for each finished puzzle.
options.zh: 表親每解一謎所得報酬。

listening.explanationZh: from solving交代樂趣來源；說話者偏好畫圖，並非全員同喜解謎。

reply.promptEn: Why do your cousins enjoy puzzle night?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼表親喜歡解謎夜？

options.en: They get their kicks from working out the hardest clues.
options.zh: 他們從解最難線索得到樂趣。

options.en: They enjoy the challenge of finding an answer together.
options.zh: 他們喜歡一起找答案的挑戰。

options.en: The difficult clues are what make the evening exciting for them.
options.zh: 難線索令那晚對他們有趣。

options.en: They find pleasure in solving something that initially seems difficult.
options.zh: 他們以解開起初看似困難的東西為樂。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回答難題帶來樂趣，沒有推成金錢或所有人相同偏好。

scene.promptZh: 朋友拍陌生人出糗放上網，旁人批評他以別人的尷尬取樂。哪句能表達這個批評？

options.en: He gets his kicks from embarrassing people in public.
options.zh: 他以令人當眾尷尬為樂。

options.en: He gets his kicks from helping people avoid attention, without filming them.
options.zh: 他以幫人避開注意為樂，也不拍他們。

options.en: He has stopped posting because he finds every part of it boring.
options.zh: 他覺得每部分都無聊，所以已停止發帖。

scene.explanationZh: 同一片語也可批評樂趣來源；負面在此活動及語氣，不是片語永遠負面。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解最不符合 get one’s kicks from？

options.en: 從解難題獲得滿足或刺激。
在輕鬆談話中說自己喜歡某種活動。
無論情境，必定表示用腳踢別人。

contrast.explanationZh: kicks在此是樂趣，不是腳部動作；是否帶批評要看活動。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我不喜歡解謎，怕你會覺得我掃興。」你喜歡畫圖，也歡迎不同參與方式。哪句回應最好？

options.en: We do not all get our kicks from the same thing; you can join the part you enjoy.
options.zh: 我們不必都從同一事得到樂趣；你可參與喜歡的部分。

options.en: You should stay with the clue-solving until you learn to enjoy that part.
options.zh: 你應一直參與解線索，直到學會喜歡那部分。

options.en: I would judge whether you fit the evening by whether you enjoy the same task as the others.
options.zh: 我會按你是否喜歡與其他人同一任務，判你適不適合那晚。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認不同偏好及自主選擇，最能回應怕掃興的顧慮；不要求先喜歡指定任務才可加入。

speaking.en: I get my kicks from finding an unexpected answer, though other people may enjoy a different part of the game.
speaking.zh: 我從找到意料外答案得到樂趣，雖然別人可能喜歡遊戲不同部分。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再以非正式口吻說自己的樂趣來源。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：同學邀你做快問快答節目的參賽者，你其實較享受在幕後設計出人意表、卻公平的題目。用一至兩句英文謝邀請，提出你更想做的角色。

examples.en: Thanks for asking, but I get my kicks from writing surprising questions rather than answering them under the lights. Could I help the team make the clues fair and interesting?
examples.zh: 謝謝邀請，但我較享受寫意外的問題，不是在燈下回答；可幫團隊把線索設計得公平有趣嗎？

examples.en: I get my kicks from creating a puzzle that makes people think. I would love to work behind the scenes on the questions, even if I do not take a contestant’s place.
examples.zh: 我享受設計令人思考的謎題；即使不當參賽者，也很想幕後協助題目。

writing.selfCheckZh: 感謝邀請，說明真正樂趣及可貢獻的幕後角色，不批評喜歡參賽的人。

takeaways.en: She gets her kicks from spotting the tiny changes between the two drawings.
takeaways.zh: 她以找出兩幅畫的細微差別為樂。

takeaways.en: We got our kicks from inventing a different ending for each puppet-show rehearsal.
takeaways.zh: 我們在每次木偶劇排練構思不同結尾，從中取樂。

lessons.titleZh: 把經驗公開展示

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: He worried that posting every trip meant putting it on display.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page133, table1, row8; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Make an experience or aspect of life visible for an audience to see.
brief.meaningZh: 把某種經驗或生活一面展示給觀眾看。
brief.grammar: put/puts/putting something on display; past put is unchanged. An experience or life is treated as something displayed; an intention to show off must be established by context.
brief.register: Conventional display wording extended to personal experience, rather than a claim that all public sharing is boastful.
brief.boundaryZh: 公開分享不自動證明虛假、炫耀或本人不享受經驗；需分可見行為與推測動機。
brief.misconceptionZh: 同一人可珍惜經驗又想與人分享，亦可選擇只給少數人看。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明展示的對象與範圍，協商自己願公開的內容。

listening.en: Posting every rehearsal felt like putting my life on display, so I chose one short clip for the public page and kept the rest for the band; I still enjoyed sharing, but wanted a boundary around it.
listening.zh: 每次排練都發帖，感覺像把生活展示出去；所以我選一短片放公開頁，其餘留樂隊看；仍喜歡分享，但想有界線。
listening.promptZh: 說話者改了甚麼分享方式？

options.en: One clip remained public, while the rest was shared within the band.
options.zh: 仍公開一短片，其餘只在樂隊內分享。

options.en: All rehearsal recordings were deleted because the speaker disliked every kind of sharing.
options.zh: 所有排練錄影都刪去，因說話者討厭任何分享。

options.en: The public page received every recording after the band was excluded.
options.zh: 樂隊被排除後，公開頁收到全部錄影。

options.en: The band asked for all recordings to be public, and the speaker agreed to post them all.
options.zh: 樂隊要求全部錄影公開，說話者也同意全部發帖。

listening.explanationZh: 選一段公開、其餘留內部，是調範圍，不是完全拒分享。

reply.promptEn: Why did you post only one rehearsal clip publicly?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼只公開一段排練短片？

options.en: Putting my life on display every time felt like more exposure than I wanted.
options.zh: 每次把生活展示出去，讓我覺公開程度超出所想。

options.en: I wanted to share something without making every rehearsal public.
options.zh: 我想分享一點，但不公開每次排練。

options.en: Keeping most recordings inside the band gave me a boundary I preferred.
options.zh: 大部分錄影留樂隊內，給我較喜歡的界線。

options.en: One clip let the audience see us while leaving some moments for the group.
options.zh: 一段短片讓觀眾看見我們，也留一些時刻給團內。

reply.explanationZh: 四句各答分享界線，沒有推成完全不享受或一定造假。

scene.promptZh: 同學公開一張比賽照，也說那天很開心；你不知道她是否想炫耀。哪句最準確？

options.en: She is putting the experience on display, but the photo alone does not tell us all her reasons for sharing it.
options.zh: 她在展示這經驗，但單憑照片未能知道分享的所有理由。

options.en: The public photo proves she did not enjoy the actual competition.
options.zh: 公開照證明她不享受真正比賽。

options.en: She kept the photograph entirely private and did not share it with anyone.
options.zh: 她把照片全留私人，沒有分享給任何人。

scene.explanationZh: 展示是可見行為，喜不喜歡活動及動機需要其他資料。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種判斷最不能只由 putting an experience on display 得出？

options.en: 某段經驗被放給觀眾看。
當事人必然只是炫耀，而且經驗一定不真實。
可再問當事人想給哪些人看。

contrast.explanationZh: 公開不等於炫耀或虛假；不要把推測動機當詞義。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「一段公開，其餘給樂隊，是不是你不再喜歡分享？」你其實只是改範圍。哪句回答最好？

options.en: I still enjoy sharing; I just do not want to keep putting my life on display after every rehearsal.
options.zh: 我仍喜歡分享，只不想每次排練後都把生活展示出去。

options.en: I should close the private band folder too, rather than leave a separate place for sharing.
options.zh: 我應連樂隊私人資料夾也關掉，不再留另一分享地方。

options.en: I would move the rest to the public page so people do not have to use two places.
options.zh: 我會把其餘也移公開頁，省得人們用兩處。

dialogue.explanationZh: 正確回應說明仍分享、只改公開範圍；全撤內部分享或為方便全公開，都沒保所想界線。

speaking.en: I enjoy sharing an experience without always putting it on display for a public audience.
speaking.zh: 我喜歡分享經驗，但不一定每次都向公開觀眾展示。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說明分享範圍及自己的選擇。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你已公開共同備賽影片，同學提醒畫面看得見他家的門牌；他原只同意分享練習，沒同意公開地址。你想道歉，先撤影片，再問遮好門牌後是否願再分享，不把原先同意擴成所有細節都可展示。用一至兩句英文回覆。

examples.en: I thought I was putting the experience on display, but I also exposed your address without asking. I am sorry; I have taken the clip down and will ask again before sharing an edited version.
examples.zh: 我以為在展示經驗，卻沒問便公開你地址；對不起，我已撤短片，再分享剪輯版前會重問。

examples.en: Putting it on display revealed more than you had agreed to share, so I have removed the video. Would you like to review a version with the house number hidden, or would you prefer that it stays offline?
examples.zh: 展示它時露出超過你同意的內容，所以我已移除影片；你想看遮好門牌版本，還是較希望不上網？

writing.selfCheckZh: 對已公開的額外資訊負責，先移除再問新版本意願；原同意練習片不代所有私人細節可公開。

takeaways.en: She chose one paragraph for the newsletter instead of putting the experience on display in every detail.
takeaways.zh: 她選一段放通訊，沒有把經驗每個細節公開展示。

takeaways.en: The public diary left him feeling that he was putting his life on display, so he changed who could read it.
takeaways.zh: 公開日記令他感到在展示生活，所以改了可閱讀的人。

lessons.titleZh: 風險帶來的尖銳緊張感

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The sharp edge of risk made the climb memorable.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page134, table1, row2; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: The intense, immediately felt aspect of uncertainty or possible loss, compared to a sharp edge.
brief.meaningZh: 把不確定或可能損失帶來的強烈切身感受，比作尖銳邊緣。
brief.grammar: the sharp edge of risk gives an experience intensity; name the actual uncertainty. This is a creative noun image, not a measurement or an established instruction to seek danger.
brief.register: Deliberate figurative description. Risk can be social or creative as well as physical; felt excitement does not prove an activity is appropriate.
brief.boundaryZh: 意象說感覺強烈，不自帶風險數字，也不表示越危險越好。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需說在意的可能後果，而不是把單純大聲或新鮮都叫風險。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體未知後果解釋緊張感，區分感受與所作選擇。

listening.en: Reading my unfinished poem to the group had a sharp edge of risk for me: they might misunderstand the ending, and I could not edit their first reaction, though I wanted to hear it.
listening.zh: 向小組讀未完成的詩，對我帶尖銳風險感：他們或誤解結尾，我也不能修改首次反應，但我想聽。
listening.promptZh: 風險感來自甚麼？

options.en: An uncertain response to unfinished writing that the speaker chose to share.
options.zh: 說話者選擇分享未完成作品後，反應仍不確定。

options.en: A guaranteed positive review already written by every listener.
options.zh: 每位聽眾已寫好保證讚賞的評語。

options.en: The speaker’s inability to hear any response because the group had left.
options.zh: 小組已離開，說話者聽不到任何回應。

options.en: A certainty that every listener would misunderstand the ending, rather than an uncertain possibility.
options.zh: 每位聽眾必誤解結尾的肯定，不是不確定可能。

listening.explanationZh: they might及不能改首次反應，支持作品被如何理解的未知，不是已保證評價。

reply.promptEn: Why did reading the unfinished poem feel especially intense?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼讀未完成的詩感覺特別強烈？

options.en: There was a sharp edge of risk in hearing an honest first response I could not control.
options.zh: 聽不能控制的真實首次反應，有尖銳風險感。

options.en: I cared about an ending that the group might read differently.
options.zh: 我在意一個小組可能有不同理解的結尾。

options.en: Sharing something unfinished left me uncertain about their reaction.
options.zh: 分享未完成的東西，令我不肯定他們的反應。

options.en: I wanted their response even though I could not decide in advance what it would be.
options.zh: 雖不能預先決定反應，我仍想聽。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答重要而不可完全控制的回應，不把風險改成保證失敗。

scene.promptZh: 陶藝者想即場改刻留作展覽的泥板；新紋一刻下去不能回復原樣，她在意可能失去原來構圖的未知。哪句最能表達這份緊張感？

options.en: The sharp edge of risk lay in changing a piece she valued without being able to restore the old pattern.
options.zh: 尖銳風險感在於改在意的作品，卻不能回復舊紋。

options.en: She was describing only how sharp the carving tool looked, not the possible loss of the original design.
options.zh: 她只在描述刻刀看來多鋒利，不是可能失去原設計。

options.en: The risk was choosing which pattern to preserve on paper, rather than changing the exhibition piece itself.
options.zh: 風險是選在紙上保留哪個紋，不是改展品本身。

scene.explanationZh: 風險是實際改刻後不能回復所珍惜構圖；不是只描述刀刃，也不只是紙上選紋的預備決定。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解最不符合 sharp edge of risk？

options.en: 某種重要的未知後果令感受鮮明。
這個意象本身已計出失敗的準確機率。
作者可用具體情況解釋緊張感。

contrast.explanationZh: 尖銳是修辭，不是機率計算，也不保證後果發生。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問：「既然讀未完成詩會緊張，不如完全不要聽回應？」你仍想得到真實第一印象。哪句最好？

options.en: That sharp edge of risk is real for me, but I still want to hear how the ending comes across.
options.zh: 對我那尖銳風險感是真實的，但我仍想聽結尾給人的感覺。

options.en: I could remove the unfamiliar ending first, so I would not be asking for a response to the part that worries me.
options.zh: 我可先刪不熟結尾，就不用問令人擔心那部分的反應。

options.en: I would ask only the people who have already read it for a first impression.
options.zh: 我會只問已讀過的人，請他們給首次印象。

dialogue.explanationZh: 本人想聽原結尾的真實首次反應；先刪那部分或只問已讀者，會失去要了解的資訊。

speaking.en: The sharp edge of risk came from sharing an unfinished idea without knowing how it would be received.
speaking.zh: 尖銳風險感來自分享未完成想法，而不知道會被怎樣接受。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說明哪個未知後果令感受強烈。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你獲邀做劇本初選評閱，才知道好友也投稿；你想參與，卻在意自己的評語可能傷友誼。你想向主辦說明這份緊張，問能否改評另一組，不把問題說成討厭讀劇本。用一至兩句英文提出。

examples.en: The sharp edge of risk for me is that judging this entry could strain a friendship, not that I dislike reading scripts. Could I assess a different group of entries and still take part?
examples.zh: 對我尖銳風險感在於評這份稿或傷友誼，不是我不喜歡讀劇本；可改評另一組，仍參與嗎？

examples.en: I feel the sharp edge of risk in having to judge a friend’s work, because the relationship matters to me. I would like to discuss another reviewing group rather than hide the connection or withdraw without explaining.
examples.zh: 需評朋友作品令我感到尖銳風險，因我在意關係；我想談改另一評閱組，不隱藏關係或沒解釋便退出。

writing.selfCheckZh: 點明未知後果是友誼受影響，坦白關係並協商另一評閱範圍；保留願參與的意願，不預判朋友必會怎樣反應。

takeaways.en: The sharp edge of risk was the possibility that the audience would hear a different story from the one I meant to tell.
takeaways.zh: 尖銳風險感在於觀眾可能聽到與我想說不同的故事。

takeaways.en: Her first live demonstration had a sharp edge of risk because she would have to answer unexpected questions.
takeaways.zh: 首次現場示範帶尖銳風險感，因她需回應意料外問題。

lessons.titleZh: 突然使人警醒、留神

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A new challenge can jolt people awake.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page134, table1, row3; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Abruptly make someone mentally alert or aware through a striking experience.
brief.meaningZh: 透過鮮明的經驗，突然令人在心智上警醒或留意。
brief.grammar: a discovery jolts/jolted someone awake; awake is the resulting awareness. Can be literal elsewhere; this lesson uses an attention metaphor.
brief.register: Productive figurative jolt + object + awake construction, not claimed as a separate fixed idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 警醒不等於已解決問題，也不一定由實際睡眠醒來；需有注意力的轉變。
brief.misconceptionZh: 突然注意到可成後續行動起點，但單一刺激未保證長期改變。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述由沒留意到突然意識到的轉折，說明接下來做甚麼。

listening.en: Seeing my own missed line in the recording jolted me awake to how often I interrupted the other actor; I began marking where to wait, rather than blaming the noisy room for every overlap.
listening.zh: 在錄影看見自己錯過的一句，令我突然意識到多常打斷另一演員；我開始標記要等的位置，不再把每次重疊都怪房間嘈吵。
listening.promptZh: 這次發現帶來甚麼轉折？

options.en: The speaker noticed a personal pattern of interrupting and began planning pauses.
options.zh: 說話者留意自己打斷別人的模式，開始規劃停頓。

options.en: The other actor was found to have interrupted every line instead.
options.zh: 反而發現另一演員每句都打斷。

options.en: The recording confirmed that room noise explained every overlap.
options.zh: 錄影確認房間嘈吵解釋每次重疊。

options.en: The speaker had been asleep during the entire rehearsal and missed every line.
options.zh: 說話者整次排練都在睡，漏掉每句。

listening.explanationZh: jolted awake是突然注意行為；marking where to wait是之後的回應，不是實際睡醒。

reply.promptEn: Why did you start marking places to pause?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你開始標記停頓的位置？

options.en: The recording jolted me awake to my habit of interrupting.
options.zh: 錄影令我突然警覺自己打斷人的習慣。

options.en: I saw that my timing was part of the problem.
options.zh: 我看見自己的時間掌握也是問題一部分。

options.en: Hearing the missed line made me reconsider how I entered the scene.
options.zh: 聽到漏掉的一句，令我重新考慮怎接入場景。

options.en: I wanted to leave space for the other actor after noticing the overlaps.
options.zh: 留意重疊後，我想留空間給另一演員。

reply.explanationZh: 四句各答新的自覺及停頓目的，不把責任全改到別人。

scene.promptZh: 學生從未看過自己影片字幕，發現一段重要資訊在靜音時全看不到，才意識到需要字幕；尚未完成修訂。哪句準確？

options.en: The silent playback jolted them awake to a gap in the information.
options.zh: 靜音重播令他們突然留意資訊的缺口。

options.en: The playback showed that the soundtrack itself was missing, rather than that information was unavailable when the sound was muted.
options.zh: 重播顯示聲軌本身缺了，不是靜音時資訊未能取得。

options.en: The students remained unaware of the missing information after watching.
options.zh: 看完後學生仍不知道資訊缺失。

scene.explanationZh: 突然注意問題與修訂已完成不同，也不是仍沒發現。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解最不符合本課 jolt someone awake？

options.en: 鮮明經驗突然令某人留意一直忽略的事。
只要被提醒，問題就必然已完全解決。
比喻中的醒覺可發生在人本來沒有睡着時。

contrast.explanationZh: 醒覺是注意轉折，不是解決結果的保證。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問：「錄影令你警醒，那下一次一定不會重疊了？」你只是剛開始標記及練等待。哪句最好？

options.en: It jolted me awake to the pattern, but I still need to practise the pauses with my partner.
options.zh: 它令我留意模式，但仍需跟同伴練停頓。

options.en: Yes, spotting the pattern is enough for me to stop rehearsing the pauses now.
options.zh: 是，留意模式已足以讓我現在停止練停頓。

options.en: I would ask for a quieter room before considering whether my timing needs work.
options.zh: 我會先要求更安靜房間，才考慮自己時間掌握是否需練。

dialogue.explanationZh: 注意到模式是練習起點；不能就停止練停頓，或先把自己已看見的時間問題擱下。

speaking.en: The unexpected example jolted me awake to something I had been overlooking, and I began to ask different questions.
speaking.zh: 意料外例子令我突然留意一直忽略的事，開始問不同問題。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說清注意力怎突然轉變及後續行動。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你要向朋友解釋為甚麼改寫故事旁白。妹妹讀後問「為甚麼每個勇敢角色都是男生？」，令你忽然留意原本沒察覺的選擇。你想謝她，說會重看人物，不把一次發現說成已完成修改。用一至兩句英文回覆。

examples.en: Your question jolted me awake to a pattern I had not noticed in the story. Thank you; I will look again at who gets to make the brave choices before I rewrite it.
examples.zh: 你的問題令我忽然留意故事中沒察覺的模式。謝謝你；重寫前我會再看由誰作勇敢選擇。

examples.en: That question jolted me awake, because I had been repeating the same kind of hero without thinking about it. I want to review the characters rather than claim the first change will solve everything.
examples.zh: 那問題令我警醒，因我一直沒多想便重複同類英雄；我想重看人物，不說首次改動便解決全部。

glossary.en: a pattern I had not noticed

writing.selfCheckZh: 謝對方帶來新發現，提出重看人物的行動，保留修改仍待做。

takeaways.en: One visitor’s question jolted us awake to the missing explanation beside the map.
takeaways.zh: 一位訪客的問題令我們突然留意地圖旁缺少的解釋。

takeaways.en: Hearing the two recordings together jolted her awake to how much the narrator’s tone changed the ending.
takeaways.zh: 把兩段錄音一起聽，令她忽然留意旁白語氣多影響結尾。

review.author: AI root

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese personally compared against each English subject, polarity, qualification and referent; no human approval claimed.

lessons.titleZh: 強烈的欣喜與亢奮

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Finishing the marathon gave her the incredible high she had hoped for.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page134, table1, row4; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: An exceptionally strong feeling of happiness or elation.
brief.meaningZh: 異常強烈的快樂或欣喜感。
brief.grammar: an incredible high; the incredible high + defining context; experience/feel/give someone a high. High is a noun here, not height or a score.
brief.register: Informal emotion noun with an intensifying adjective; not a separately fixed idiom. Context distinguishes elation from intoxicant senses of high.
brief.boundaryZh: 強烈高興不表示結果完美或感受永遠持續；此課不把high當高度或分數。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需分當下的欣喜及稍後的情緒，不用短暫失落抹去曾經快樂。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述欣喜的時點與原因，並自然安排接下來的節奏。

listening.en: Hearing the audience sing our last chorus gave me an incredible high; on the quiet bus home I felt tired and ordinary again, but that did not make the shared moment any less special.
listening.zh: 聽觀眾唱最後副歌令我極欣喜；回家巴士安靜時又覺疲倦平凡，但不減那共同一刻的特別。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣形容情緒的先後？

options.en: A powerful happy moment was followed by tiredness, without being dismissed as meaningless.
options.zh: 強烈快樂後是疲倦，但沒有把原來一刻說成無意義。

options.en: The whole bus journey kept the same intense excitement without any change.
options.zh: 整段巴士旅程都維持同樣亢奮，沒有轉變。

options.en: The audience never joined in, so the speaker’s happiness came from singing alone.
options.zh: 觀眾沒加入，所以快樂來自獨唱。

options.en: The strongest happiness came during the bus journey rather than the shared chorus.
options.zh: 最強烈快樂發生在巴士旅程，不是在共同副歌中。

listening.explanationZh: an incredible high指強烈欣喜；後來平靜疲倦不否定共同演唱的價值。

reply.promptEn: Why was that last chorus so memorable for you?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼最後副歌對你那麼難忘？

options.en: Singing it with the audience gave me an incredible high.
options.zh: 與觀眾合唱令我極欣喜。

options.en: I felt a strong burst of joy when their voices joined ours.
options.zh: 他們的聲音加入時，我感到強烈喜悅。

options.en: Sharing the song made that part of the evening especially happy.
options.zh: 分享歌曲令那晚這部分特別快樂。

options.en: The response from the room meant a great deal to me at that moment.
options.zh: 房內的回應當刻對我意義很大。

reply.explanationZh: 四句皆說觀眾加入帶來的強烈感受，不把高興改成分數或永恆狀態。

scene.promptZh: 學生完成首次自編廣播，開播一刻非常興奮，但知道仍有發音要改。哪句貼切？

options.en: The first broadcast gave her an incredible high, even though she could still hear things to improve.
options.zh: 首次廣播令她極欣喜，雖仍聽到可改善之處。

options.en: Her excitement was only about the flawless pronunciation, rather than hearing the programme broadcast for the first time.
options.zh: 她只因發音完美而興奮，不是因首次聽節目播出。

options.en: The student’s main feeling about the launch was disappointment; the improvements mattered more than the happy first broadcast.
options.zh: 學生對開播主要感失望；改善處比首次廣播的快樂更重要。

scene.explanationZh: 欣喜與知道可改善並存，不是品質已完美或不能快樂。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解最不符合本課 an incredible high？

options.en: 某段經驗帶來強烈欣喜。
是情緒名詞，不是這裏的實際高度。
高興必定永久持續，之後不可能疲倦。

contrast.explanationZh: 強烈不等於永久，還需看前後情況。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友問：「巴士上很安靜，是不是剛才合唱其實不好玩？」你只是在回復平常、也累了。哪句最好？

options.en: It gave me an incredible high; I am just tired now, and I still treasure that moment.
options.zh: 剛才令我極欣喜，只是現在累了，仍珍惜那一刻。

options.en: I should repeat the concert immediately so I do not have to let the excitement settle.
options.zh: 我應立即再演，這樣不用讓興奮平復。

options.en: I would judge how much the evening mattered by how energetic I feel on the bus.
options.zh: 我會按巴士上多有精神，判那晚對我多重要。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認當時欣喜與現在疲倦最貼合問題；立即重演或用現時精神評整晚，沒有分清感受先後。

speaking.en: The shared applause gave me an incredible high, though I was ready for a quiet evening afterwards.
speaking.zh: 共同掌聲令我極欣喜，但之後我想安靜度過晚上。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再描述強烈欣喜及其後的感受。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友想在你首次劇本讀演成功後即晚開下一個大項目會議。你很高興，也想先休息一天整理觀眾回應。用一至兩句英文回覆，保留合作意願。

examples.en: The reading gave me an incredible high, and I do want to work together again. Could we leave a day to rest and read the audience’s notes before planning the next project?
examples.zh: 讀演令我極欣喜，也確想再合作；可先留一天休息及讀觀眾筆記，再計劃下一項目嗎？

examples.en: I am still enjoying the incredible high of hearing the script performed, but I would like a quieter day before another meeting. Let us compare the feedback tomorrow and then choose a time to plan.
examples.zh: 我仍享受聽劇本演出的欣喜，但再開會前想安靜一天；明天先比回應，再選規劃時間吧。

writing.selfCheckZh: 肯定強烈喜悅及再合作意願，協商休息和整理回應的先後。

takeaways.en: The final bow brought an incredible high after weeks of rehearsing in an empty room.
takeaways.zh: 數周在空房間排練後，最後謝幕帶來強烈欣喜。

takeaways.en: She remembered the incredible high of hearing her first story read on the school radio.
takeaways.zh: 她記得首篇故事在校園廣播讀出時的強烈欣喜。

lessons.titleZh: 試探自己能做到的程度

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Experienced climbers sometimes test their limits.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page134, table1, row6; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Try to discover the extent of one’s abilities or endurance.
brief.meaningZh: 嘗試了解自己的能力或耐力可到甚麼程度。
brief.grammar: test one’s limits; tested/testing; specify the ability being explored. Testing a limit is different from necessarily exceeding it.
brief.register: Conventional ability-boundary metaphor.
brief.boundaryZh: 不表示必須超越所有界限，也不等於測試已證能處理任何任務。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可以循序挑戰、按結果調整；測試不是不理限制的保證。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說清正在探索哪種能力，按經驗作下一步選擇。

listening.en: I tested my limits by telling a longer story without my usual notes; I managed the opening, then lost the order near the end, which showed me where I needed another rehearsal.
listening.zh: 我不靠平常筆記講較長故事，試探能力；開頭做到，結尾附近次序亂了，讓我知道哪裏需再排練。
listening.promptZh: 這次嘗試讓說話者知道甚麼？

options.en: Which part could be managed and which still needed rehearsal.
options.zh: 哪部分做到，哪部分仍需排練。

options.en: That notes had been used for every line of the longer story.
options.zh: 較長故事每句都用了筆記。

options.en: That the whole story had been told smoothly from beginning to end.
options.zh: 整個故事由頭到尾都順暢講完。

options.en: That a shorter story was required because the longer version had never been attempted.
options.zh: 因從未試較長版，所以需講較短故事。

listening.explanationZh: 開頭做到及後段失次序，提供能力界線的資訊，不是全已熟練。

reply.promptEn: Why did you try the longer story without your usual notes?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼不靠平常筆記試講較長故事？

options.en: I wanted to test my limits and find where another rehearsal would help.
options.zh: 我想試探能力，找哪裏再排練會有用。

options.en: The attempt could show me how far I could keep the order in my head.
options.zh: 嘗試可讓我知道能在腦中維持多少次序。

options.en: I wanted to learn which parts I could manage without that support.
options.zh: 我想知道沒有那支援可處理哪些部分。

options.en: Trying a more demanding version gave me a clearer starting point for practice.
options.zh: 試較有要求版本，讓我較清楚練習起點。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均說探索能力的目的，沒有把嘗試當保證全成功。

scene.promptZh: 莉莉已能畫小速寫，今次試較大紙張；途中發現構圖要重排，決定先改草圖。哪句貼切？

options.en: The larger drawing tested her limits and helped her see what to practise next.
options.zh: 較大畫作試探她的能力，幫她看見之後練甚麼。

options.en: She avoided every new demand by drawing the same small sketch again.
options.zh: 她再畫同一小速寫，避開每項新要求。

options.en: The larger attempt showed that colour mixing, rather than the arrangement of the drawing, needed her next attention.
options.zh: 較大嘗試顯示接着需留意的是調色，不是畫面安排。

scene.explanationZh: 新尺寸及發現需改，正是探索能力；未全完成不等於沒試。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論最不宜由 test one’s limits 得出？

options.en: 嘗試可幫人了解能力範圍。
每次測試都必須超越全部限制才算成功。
結果可顯示仍需練習的部分。

contrast.explanationZh: 探索本身可得資訊，並不要求每次超越所有限制。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「結尾忘了次序，這次就白試吧？」你正想以此安排排練。哪句最好？

options.en: Testing my limits showed me where the order breaks down; I can practise that section next.
options.zh: 試探能力讓我知道次序在哪斷；接着可練該段。

options.en: I will rehearse only the opening again, because it is the part that already feels comfortable.
options.zh: 我會只再練開頭，因那部分已較自在。

options.en: I would shorten the ending before checking exactly where I lost the sequence.
options.zh: 我會先縮短結尾，才查究竟在哪失次序。

dialogue.explanationZh: 嘗試已定位後段問題，針對該處再練才利用結果；只練舒服開頭或未查就刪，會錯過診斷資訊。

speaking.en: I wanted to test my limits, then use what happened to choose a useful next step.
speaking.zh: 我想試探能力，再按發生的情況選有用下一步。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說明試哪項能力及怎用結果。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友邀你獨自主持整晚讀書會，你想先主持開場十分鐘，了解自己怎回應即場問題，之後再談更長時段。用一至兩句英文協商。

examples.en: I would like to test my limits with the first ten minutes before taking the whole evening. Could you stay for the questions so we can discuss what I need to practise afterwards?
examples.zh: 我想先主持首十分鐘試探能力，再接整晚；你可留下聽問題，好讓之後討論需練甚麼嗎？

examples.en: Let me test my limits by leading the opening discussion, rather than promise the entire session yet. We can review how I handle questions before deciding on a longer role.
examples.zh: 讓我主持開場討論試探能力，暫不承諾全場；可先看我怎回問題，再決定較長角色。

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出有範圍的嘗試、觀察問題回應及之後評估，不因試能力就先承諾全晚。

takeaways.en: Writing a scene with no dialogue tested her limits and changed how she used small gestures.
takeaways.zh: 寫沒有對白的場景試探她的能力，也改變怎運用小動作。

takeaways.en: He tested his limits by explaining the project without slides, then asked which part needed a clearer example.
takeaways.zh: 他不靠投影片解釋項目試探能力，再問哪部分需較清楚例子。

lessons.titleZh: 進入人生新階段的經歷

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Moving away for university felt like a rite of passage.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page134, table1, row9; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: An event or experience seen as marking entry into a new stage of life or a new social role.
brief.meaningZh: 被視為標誌進入人生新階段或新社會角色的事件或經歷。
brief.grammar: an experience is/feels like a rite of passage for someone; a rite has an initial consonant sound despite written rite. Can name a formal ceremony or a figuratively significant transition.
brief.register: Established expression with ceremonial and wider figurative uses.
brief.boundaryZh: 重要轉變不代表人人都必經同一事件，也不以某人的經歷判所有人是否成熟。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需說誰把甚麼當新階段標誌；平常小事不因先後發生便自動成儀式。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋轉折的個人或社群意義，尊重不同成長路徑。

listening.en: Cooking the festival meal with my mother felt like a rite of passage when she asked me to lead the preparations for the first time; I was taking a family role, not simply learning another recipe.
listening.zh: 母親首次請我帶領節慶備餐時，一起煮飯像進入新階段；我是在接家庭角色，不只學另一食譜。
listening.promptZh: 這經歷為甚麼像人生轉折？

options.en: Leading the preparations marked a new family role for the speaker.
options.zh: 帶領備餐標誌說話者的新家庭角色。

options.en: Every family had agreed that the same meal was a compulsory test of adulthood.
options.zh: 每個家庭已同意同一餐是強制成年測試。

options.en: The mother kept all responsibility and asked the speaker only to watch again.
options.zh: 母親保留全部責任，只請說話者再旁觀。

options.en: The speaker was describing a recipe with no connection to a change of role.
options.zh: 說話者在描述與角色轉變無關的食譜。

listening.explanationZh: for the first time接帶領責任，賦予新階段意義；不是替所有家庭定成年條件。

reply.promptEn: Why did preparing that meal feel different this year?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼今年備餐感覺不同？

options.en: Leading it felt like a rite of passage into a more responsible family role.
options.zh: 帶領它像進入較有責任家庭角色的轉折。

options.en: My mother was trusting me with preparations I had not led before.
options.zh: 母親把以前沒帶領過的準備交給我。

options.en: I was moving from helping with a recipe to organising the meal.
options.zh: 我由幫一道食譜，轉為統籌餐食。

options.en: The responsibility gave the familiar activity a new meaning for me.
options.zh: 這責任給熟悉活動新的個人意義。

reply.explanationZh: 四句皆說角色與信任的改變，不把餐食本身當普遍成熟門檻。

scene.promptZh: 學徒首次獨立接待一位客人，師傅在旁可支援；她把那天看作由旁觀到承擔工作的轉折。哪句貼切？

options.en: That first appointment felt like a rite of passage for her.
options.zh: 首次接待對她像進入新階段的經歷。

options.en: She was only repeating a task with no change in her role as an observer.
options.zh: 她只重複任務，旁觀角色沒變。

options.en: The appointment marked the end of every supervised task, rather than her first independent responsibility with help nearby.
options.zh: 這接待標誌所有受指導任務的終結，不是有附近支援下首次獨立負責。

scene.explanationZh: 以首次承擔新角色支持轉折意義，無需人人一樣。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解最不符合 a rite of passage？

options.en: 某個人或社群用一經驗標誌新階段。
有時是正式儀式，有時是具轉折意義的經驗。
所有人必須經歷完全相同事件才算成長。

contrast.explanationZh: 片語標示轉折，不規定所有人成長路徑相同。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我沒主持過家庭大餐，是不是少了一個必經成長關卡？」你說的是自己的角色轉變。哪句最好？

options.en: It was a rite of passage for me, but your own changes may be marked by different experiences.
options.zh: 對我那是轉折，但你的變化可由不同經歷標示。

options.en: I would compare your progress with mine by whether you have led that same meal yet.
options.zh: 我會按你是否已帶同一餐食，比你我的成長進度。

options.en: Perhaps you need the same family role before looking for a different kind of milestone.
options.zh: 也許你需先做同一家庭角色，才找別種里程碑。

dialogue.explanationZh: 個人轉折不必複製他人的事件或次序；最好回應肯定不同經歷的成長意義。

speaking.en: It felt like a rite of passage because I was trusted with a role I had only watched before.
speaking.zh: 那像進入新階段，因我獲信任承擔以前只旁觀的角色。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再連結具體事件與新階段的意義。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你首次以校刊編輯身份接收新同學投稿，想在日記記下從只寫自己作品，轉為照顧別人文字的感受。用一至兩句英文寫這個轉折，不宣稱只有當編輯才算成熟。

examples.en: Reading the first submission as an editor felt like a rite of passage: I was responsible for someone else’s words as well as my own. I wanted to earn that trust by listening before suggesting changes.
examples.zh: 以編輯身份讀首份來稿，像進入新階段：我不只為自己，也為別人的文字負責；我想先聽再提修改，配得上信任。

examples.en: Accepting a new writer’s story was a rite of passage for me, from protecting my own draft to helping another voice be heard. It made me think differently about the trust behind an edit.
examples.zh: 接新作者故事對我是轉折，由保自己初稿，變幫另一聲音被聽見；令我重新想編輯背後的信任。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以接收別人作品的新責任寫日記轉折，保個人路徑而非普遍成年門檻。

takeaways.en: Her first turn leading the neighbourhood walk became a rite of passage into the organising team.
takeaways.zh: 首次帶領街坊散步，成為她進入籌辦團隊的轉折。

takeaways.en: For him, handing a finished key to the new tenant felt like a rite of passage into working life.
takeaways.zh: 對他而言，把完成的鑰匙交新租客，像進入工作生活的轉折。

lessons.titleZh: 腦內對自己說的想法

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The beginners ignored the voice inside their head that said the climb was impossible.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page134, table1, row10; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: One’s own inner thoughts or self-talk, personified as a voice.
brief.meaningZh: 把自己的內在想法或自我對話，擬作一把聲音。
brief.grammar: the voice inside my/her/their head said/told...; the possessive identifies whose thought it is. Its message may be doubtful, encouraging or mistaken.
brief.register: Conventional inner-speech metaphor in ordinary narration; this lesson describes thoughts, not a diagnosis or a report about an external speaker.
brief.boundaryZh: 內心想法不等於事實或他人的意見，也不是每次都負面。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需分人物想到的話、實際有人說的話，以及行動後得到的新資訊。
brief.outcomeZh: 能引用自己的自我對話，選擇回應而不把念頭當保證。

listening.en: The voice inside my head said the audience would notice every pause, but the first listener asked about the story instead; I began to separate my prediction from what people actually told me.
listening.zh: 腦內的聲音說觀眾會留意每次停頓，但首位聽眾反而問故事；我開始分自己的預測與別人真正說的話。
listening.promptZh: 說話者在分清甚麼？

options.en: An inner prediction about pauses and an actual listener’s interest in the story.
options.zh: 自己對停頓的預測，及真正聽眾對故事的興趣。

options.en: A direct warning every audience member had spoken aloud before the talk.
options.zh: 演講前每位觀眾都親口說的警告。

options.en: The listener’s request that all pauses be removed before any story could be heard.
options.zh: 聽眾要求刪掉所有停頓才可聽故事。

options.en: A prediction that was confirmed because nobody asked about the story.
options.zh: 因沒人問故事而被證實的預測。

listening.explanationZh: 聲音是自我預測；首位聽眾的實際問題提供不同資訊。

reply.promptEn: Why did you reconsider your worry about the pauses?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你重新考慮對停頓的擔心？

options.en: The voice inside my head had predicted something the first listener did not focus on.
options.zh: 腦內聲音預測的事，不是首位聽眾關注的事。

options.en: The listener asked about the story rather than criticising my timing.
options.zh: 聽眾問故事，不是批評我的時間掌握。

options.en: My thought about what people would notice was not the same as their spoken response.
options.zh: 我想到人會留意甚麼，與他們親口回應不同。

options.en: The first question gave me a reason to look beyond my own prediction.
options.zh: 首個問題給我理由，不只看自己的預測。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都分自我對話與已聽到回應，沒有保證後面所有人怎想。

scene.promptZh: 人物出門前在心中提醒自己「先聽完整個問題」，並沒有人在房中對她說話。哪句準確？

options.en: The voice inside her head reminded her to listen before answering.
options.zh: 她腦內聲音提醒先聽再答。

options.en: A person in the room had given her a spoken instruction.
options.zh: 房中有人親口給她指示。

options.en: She was planning the words of her next spoken answer rather than reminding herself to listen to the whole question.
options.zh: 她在計劃接着親口回答的字句，不是提醒自己聽完整個問題。

scene.explanationZh: 這裏是她自己對聆聽方式的提醒，不是房內別人的指示，也不是已在擬下一回答；內在聲音未必只表恐懼。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解最不宜由 the voice inside someone’s head 這個敘事比喻推出？

options.en: 作者在描寫人物的自我對話。
這想法一定是真相，而且人人都同意。
人物可選擇如何回應自己的念頭。

contrast.explanationZh: 比喻中的念頭仍可能錯，亦不代表別人的共識。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「你腦內已覺得大家只聽停頓，為甚麼還看回應？」你想分預測及觀察。哪句最好？

options.en: The voice inside my head is only one thought; I want to hear what the listeners actually say.
options.zh: 腦內聲音只是一個想法；我想聽聽眾真正說甚麼。

options.en: I should look only for comments about pauses and put the questions about the story aside.
options.zh: 我應只找停頓評語，把故事問題放旁邊。

options.en: I would ask them whether my prediction is right before letting them give an open response.
options.zh: 我會先問預測是否對，才讓他們自由回應。

dialogue.explanationZh: 應聽實際開放回應，不只找符合原擔心的評語，或先用預測收窄別人可說甚麼。

speaking.en: The voice inside my head was making a prediction, so I decided to listen to the response before treating it as fact.
speaking.zh: 腦內聲音是在預測，所以我決定先聽回應，才把它當事實。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分人物的內在想法與可觀察的回應。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你刪了給朋友的邀請草稿，因心裏總想「她一定嫌麻煩」。她未看過，也未說不想去。用一至兩句英文向同伴說明，你會先問朋友意願，不替她決定。

examples.en: The voice inside my head keeps saying she will find the invitation a nuisance, but I have not asked her. I will send a simple message and let her decide whether she wants to come.
examples.zh: 腦內聲音一直說她會嫌邀請麻煩，但我未問她；我會發簡單訊息，讓她決定是否想來。

examples.en: I have been treating the voice inside my head as if it were her answer. Instead of deleting another draft, I will ask what she would enjoy and leave room for her to say no.
examples.zh: 我一直把腦內聲音當她的答案；不再刪另一初稿，我會問她喜歡甚麼，也留空間讓她拒絕。

glossary.en: room for her to say no

writing.selfCheckZh: 把擔心說成自己的預測，提出真正詢問及容許拒絕，不保證朋友必答應。

takeaways.en: The voice inside his head urged him to rush, but he chose to read the question once more.
takeaways.zh: 他腦內聲音催快，但他選擇再讀問題一次。

takeaways.en: She answered the voice inside her head with a reminder that one unfinished sketch was not her whole body of work.
takeaways.zh: 她提醒自己，一幅未完成速寫不等於全部作品，回應腦內聲音。

lessons.titleZh: 跨過心裏的一道障礙

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: climbed over a piece of themselves
sources.sentence: After the climb, the team felt they had climbed over a piece of themselves.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page134, table1, row11; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Overcome an internal fear or self-imposed obstacle, imagined as something one can climb over.
brief.meaningZh: 把克服內在恐懼或自己設的障礙，想像為跨過一道阻隔。
brief.grammar: climb/climbed over an inner barrier; name the particular fear. A transparent production version of the source’s more opaque climbing-over-part-of-oneself image.
brief.register: Creative metaphor, not an established fixed idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 跨過某一心理障礙不表示所有疑慮消失，也不是實際跨越身體的一部分。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需用具體選擇說明內在改變，勿把勇氣寫成永久無所畏懼。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把一項內在顧慮連到具體行動，保留仍在學習的部分。

listening.en: Asking my former classmate to read the draft felt like climbing over an inner barrier; I had feared seeming inexperienced, but now I could ask one honest question without pretending the whole story was finished.
listening.zh: 請舊同學讀初稿，像跨過內在障礙；我怕顯得沒經驗，現在卻可真誠問一個問題，不用裝整個故事已完成。
listening.promptZh: 跨過的是哪道障礙？

options.en: The fear of appearing inexperienced when asking for a response to unfinished work.
options.zh: 就未完成作品求回應時，怕顯得沒經驗的顧慮。

options.en: A wall blocking the classmate’s entrance to the room.
options.zh: 擋住同學入房的牆。

options.en: The classmate’s judgement mattered less than avoiding any question about the unfinished draft.
options.zh: 比起避開任何未完成初稿的問題，同學評價較不重要。

options.en: A classmate had already rewritten the ending, so the speaker needed no questions.
options.zh: 同學已重寫結尾，所以說話者不需提問。

listening.explanationZh: 內在顧慮是求回應時怕顯沒經驗；現在能真誠問初稿問題，不是跨實體牆，也不是繼續避所有問題。

reply.promptEn: Why did asking your classmate to read the draft matter to you?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼請同學讀初稿對你重要？

options.en: It felt like climbing over an inner barrier about appearing inexperienced.
options.zh: 那像跨過怕顯沒經驗的內在障礙。

options.en: I could ask for an honest response instead of pretending I needed none.
options.zh: 我可求真實回應，不用裝作不需要。

options.en: I was letting someone see the unfinished work despite my hesitation.
options.zh: 雖猶豫，我仍讓人看未完成作品。

options.en: Making that request changed how I dealt with my fear of being judged.
options.zh: 提出請求改變了我怎面對被評判的恐懼。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以求回應的行動解釋內在轉折，不把故事已完成當條件。

scene.promptZh: 人物首次願意承認自己不懂一個詞，並請朋友解釋；她仍會緊張，但不再只點頭裝懂。哪句貼切？

options.en: She climbed over an inner barrier by asking the question she had been hiding.
options.zh: 她問出一直藏着的問題，跨過內在障礙。

options.en: She avoided the question and continued pretending to understand.
options.zh: 她避開問題，繼續裝懂。

options.en: She asked only how to pronounce the word, while its meaning had already been clear to her.
options.zh: 她只問怎讀那詞，意思原已清楚。

scene.explanationZh: 具體改變是願問，不是全知或繼續迴避；仍緊張不否定一步改變。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解最不符合此處 climb over an inner barrier？

options.en: 以跨障礙意象形容面對特定顧慮。
必須真的從身體某一部分上方爬過。
人物可仍有別的疑慮或學習需要。

contrast.explanationZh: 內在障礙是恐懼的比喻，不是身體動作。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「你終於肯給人看初稿，現在應該再沒疑慮了？」你只是不再假裝不需回應。哪句最好？

options.en: I have climbed over an inner barrier about asking, but I still feel nervous about sharing some parts.
options.zh: 我跨過提問的內在障礙，但分享某些部分仍緊張。

options.en: I should wait until I feel no nerves before showing another unfinished scene.
options.zh: 我應等到完全不緊張，才展示另一未完成場景。

options.en: I would choose only the least important question next time so I do not have to share the work I care about.
options.zh: 下次我會只選最不重要的問題，就不需分享在意的作品。

dialogue.explanationZh: 跨一障礙與仍緊張可並存；等待全無感覺或只問無關緊要的事，沒有直接澄清當前感受。

speaking.en: I climbed over an inner barrier when I asked for help instead of pretending I already knew the answer.
speaking.zh: 我求助而不裝作已知答案時，跨過一道內在障礙。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再以一個實際選擇說明內在改變。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你先前未核群組訊息，就當眾指責朋友沒有交資料，後來發現自己漏看附件。你一直怕承認錯會丟面子，現在想跨過這個心裏障礙，直接向朋友道歉，並徵詢是否可在原群組更正。用一至兩句英文寫道歉訊息。

examples.en: Admitting that I blamed you before checking the messages feels like climbing over an inner barrier, but I owe you an apology. May I correct what I told the group and explain that I missed the attachment?
examples.zh: 承認未核訊息便怪你，像跨過心裏障礙，但我應向你道歉。我可否更正在群組說的話，解釋是我漏看附件？

examples.en: I climbed over an inner barrier when I accepted that my accusation was unfair. I am sorry, and I would like to put the record right in the group if you are comfortable with that.
examples.zh: 承認自己的指責不公平時，我跨過了一個心裏障礙。對不起；若你願意，我想在群組更正事實。

writing.selfCheckZh: 指出怕丟面子與承認指責錯誤的轉變，直接道歉並商量更正；不把願道歉當對方已原諒。

takeaways.en: She climbed over an inner barrier when she invited criticism of the scene she cared about most.
takeaways.zh: 她邀人批評最在意的場景時，跨過內在障礙。

takeaways.en: He was still hesitant, but asking his partner to slow down felt like climbing over an inner barrier.
takeaways.zh: 他仍猶豫，但請同伴放慢，感覺像跨內在障礙。

lessons.titleZh: 不惜任何代價

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Freedom should not come at any price.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page135, table1, row2; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Regardless of the cost or consequences in pursuing a desired result.
brief.meaningZh: 為追求想要的結果，不論付出甚麼代價或後果。
brief.grammar: want/pursue success at any price; want X, but not at any price sets a limit on acceptable costs. Do not confuse with come at a price meaning have a cost.
brief.register: Established idiom; price may include trust, time or relationships as well as money.
brief.boundaryZh: 不一定是標價；拒絕不惜代價，不等於拒絕目標本身。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需保留否定範圍：想達目標但不願以任何手段達成。
brief.outcomeZh: 能表達追求目標及不接受的代價，提出另一做法。

listening.en: I wanted the prize, but not at any price: when the team suggested hiding our partner’s contribution, I chose to credit her even if it meant sharing the award.
listening.zh: 我想得獎，但不願不惜任何代價：團隊提議隱去伙伴貢獻，我仍選給她名分，即使要分享獎項。
listening.promptZh: 說話者對獎項及代價的態度是甚麼？

options.en: The prize mattered, but claiming another person’s work was an unacceptable way to obtain it.
options.zh: 獎項重要，但把別人工作據為己有不是可接受方法。

options.en: The speaker had no interest in any prize and refused to enter the project.
options.zh: 說話者對任何獎項沒興趣，拒絕參加項目。

options.en: The partner agreed that her work should be hidden so the speaker could win alone.
options.zh: 伙伴同意隱去工作，好讓說話者獨得獎。

options.en: The decision concerned only the cash price of entering the award.
options.zh: 決定只關乎報獎的現金費用。

listening.explanationZh: wanted與but not並存，拒絕的是抹他人貢獻的代價，不是獎項一切價值。

reply.promptEn: Why did you name your partner despite wanting the prize?
reply.promptZh: 你想得獎，為甚麼仍列伙伴名字？

options.en: I wanted to win, but not at any price.
options.zh: 我想贏，但不願不惜任何代價。

options.en: Giving proper credit mattered more than receiving the whole award alone.
options.zh: 適當給名分比獨得整個獎重要。

options.en: I did not want a result that depended on hiding her work.
options.zh: 我不想結果要靠隱去她工作。

options.en: Sharing recognition was a cost I preferred to misrepresenting the project.
options.zh: 與其失實呈現項目，我寧願分享認可。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答界線與公平認可，不把拒代價誤成從不想贏。

scene.promptZh: 學生想當選班代表，但拒絕散播對手未核實的傳聞，提議只談自己的計劃。哪句貼切？

options.en: She wants to be elected, but not at any price.
options.zh: 她想當選，但不願不惜任何代價。

options.en: She wants election at any price, including spreading the rumour she has refused to use.
options.zh: 她不惜代價想當選，包括散播已拒用的傳聞。

options.en: She has decided not to seek election or discuss any plan.
options.zh: 她已決定不參選，也不談任何計劃。

scene.explanationZh: 願參選與拒不當手段可並存，不是要傳謠或已退選。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解最不符合「I want it, but not at any price」？

options.en: 想要結果，但有不能接受的代價。
願意不論後果，用任何手段取得它。
可尋找尊重原有界線的另一條路。

contrast.explanationZh: but not否定無限代價，不能漏否定讀成任何手段都接受。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說：「不肯隱去伙伴名字，即是你不想贏吧？」你仍願參賽。哪句回答最好？

options.en: I do want to win, but not at any price; let us submit the project with everyone credited.
options.zh: 我確想贏，但不是不惜代價；一起把每人列名再交項目吧。

options.en: Could we leave her name off the shortlist version and add it only if we win?
options.zh: 可先不把她名放入圍版本，贏了才加嗎？

options.en: I would send a single-name entry first and ask about shared credit afterwards.
options.zh: 我會先交單人署名，再問共同認可。

dialogue.explanationZh: 已知界線是尊重貢獻，延後或只得獎才署名仍違背它；最好回應保參賽與共同認可。

speaking.en: I want the opportunity, but not at any price; the way we reach it matters to me too.
speaking.zh: 我想要機會，但不願不惜代價；怎樣得到也對我重要。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再保留想達目標與拒絕某些代價的分別。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你想接學生藝術展的統籌職務，但要求每天放學後留校整個月，會令你無法履行已答應家人的照顧安排。你不想只為得到職銜便作不能履行的承諾，想問可否共同統籌；若不行，願找較小職務。用一至兩句英文回覆邀請者。

examples.en: I would like to coordinate the exhibition, but not at any price: I cannot abandon the care arrangement I have already agreed. Could we discuss a shared role, or a smaller responsibility if daily attendance is essential?
examples.zh: 我想統籌展覽，但不是不惜任何代價；我不能放棄已答應的照顧安排。可否談共同統籌，若每天出席不可少，就改談較小職務？

examples.en: Taking the title at any price would mean promising time I cannot give. I am still interested in helping, so I would like to ask whether the coordination can be shared before accepting.
examples.zh: 不惜代價接下職銜，會變成答應自己給不了的時間。我仍有興趣幫忙，所以接受前想問能否分擔統籌。

writing.selfCheckZh: 保留想參與的目標，也說清不能犧牲的已有承諾，詢問共享或較小職務；不把拒絕某代價說成不想幫忙，亦不先承諾做不到的時數。

takeaways.en: She wanted a place in the show, but not at any price, so she refused to take credit for someone else’s design.
takeaways.zh: 她想參演，但不願不惜代價，所以拒把別人設計據為己有。

takeaways.en: The club pursued publicity at any price until members questioned what that approach was doing to their trust.
takeaways.zh: 俱樂部不惜代價求宣傳，直到成員質疑這方式怎影響信任。

lessons.titleZh: 拿某事冒險、碰運氣

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: We cannot roll the dice on public safety.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page135, table1, row4; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Take a chance on an uncertain outcome instead of securing what matters.
brief.meaningZh: 面對不確定結果，把重要的事交給運氣。
brief.grammar: roll the dice on + outcome/resource; rolled/rolling; name what is being put at risk. Dice are a gambling metaphor here.
brief.register: Informal risk metaphor, often critical when the possible loss matters to other people.
brief.boundaryZh: 不一定真賭錢；有不確定性不代表任何選擇都等於盲目冒險，需看有否可用核查。
brief.misconceptionZh: 指出可避免的未知，不把曾經順利當今次保證，也不說有風險就永不能做。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋不願碰運氣的是甚麼，提出針對性的核查或替代。

listening.en: We would be rolling the dice on the show’s opening if we assumed the borrowed projector would take our file; nobody had tried it, so we arranged a short playback before printing the final running order.
listening.zh: 若假定借來投影機可播檔案，就是拿演出開場碰運氣；沒人試過，所以我們安排短播，再印最後流程。
listening.promptZh: 團隊想避免哪項賭運氣？

options.en: Relying on untested playback for the opening when a check could be arranged.
options.zh: 明可安排核查，卻把開場寄託在未試的播放。

options.en: Repeating a check that had already confirmed this exact file on that projector.
options.zh: 重做已確認這檔案在該機播放的核查。

options.en: Choosing the final running order before any projector had been borrowed.
options.zh: 尚未借投影機便選最後流程。

options.en: Holding a dice game for the audience instead of showing a film.
options.zh: 不播片而為觀眾舉行骰子遊戲。

listening.explanationZh: if we assumed及nobody had tried界定未核假設，之後短播處理該未知。

reply.promptEn: Why did you arrange a short playback first?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼先安排短暫試播？

options.en: We did not want to roll the dice on the opening by trusting an untested file.
options.zh: 我們不想靠未試檔案，拿開場碰運氣。

options.en: The borrowed projector had not yet been checked with our file.
options.zh: 借來投影機尚未用我們檔案核過。

options.en: A quick check could answer the question before the final order was printed.
options.zh: 印最後流程前，快速核查可解答那問題。

options.en: Assuming it would work left an avoidable uncertainty at the start of the show.
options.zh: 假定能播，會讓開場留可避免的未知。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明未試兼容性及可做的核查，不是否定整個演出。

scene.promptZh: 作者保留原稿後，讓三位願試讀的朋友比較兩個新結尾，隨時可改回；她想說有不確定性，卻不想把這次試驗說成拿唯一整本作品孤注一擲。哪句最準確？

options.en: She is testing an uncertain ending with a saved draft, rather than rolling the dice on the only copy of her novel.
options.zh: 她有保留初稿，正試不確定結尾，不是拿唯一小說副本碰運氣。

options.en: She has given up the original and cannot recover it if the new ending fails.
options.zh: 她已放棄原稿，新結尾不合也無法恢復。

options.en: She plans to publish the new ending as final before hearing from any reader.
options.zh: 她計劃未聽任何讀者回應，便把新結尾當定稿出版。

scene.explanationZh: 承認試驗仍有未知，也保留原稿及先比較回應的條件；不能抹掉可回復或未定稿的範圍。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解最不符合此處 roll the dice on？

options.en: 拿重要結果冒一個未處理的風險。
必須真的拿骰子作決定，否則不能用。
語境可表達對碰運氣做法的擔憂。

contrast.explanationZh: 此處借骰子說不確定風險，不需真有骰子。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說：「上次播到，今次不用試吧？」你們今次換了投影機。哪句最好？

options.en: That was another projector; I would rather test this one than roll the dice on the opening.
options.zh: 那是另一部；我寧願試這部，不拿開場碰運氣。

options.en: I would rely on the last screening until a problem actually appears on the new projector.
options.zh: 我會先靠上次放映，直到新機真出問題再說。

options.en: I would check the title’s font first and leave the playback question until the audience arrives.
options.zh: 我會先核片名字體，播放問題留觀眾到才處理。

dialogue.explanationZh: 今次換機造成具體待核問題，先試播才回應它；靠不同舊機或先看字體都沒有處理兼容性。

speaking.en: I would rather check the uncertain part than roll the dice on an outcome that matters to the whole group.
speaking.zh: 我寧願核不確定部分，不把全組重視的結果交給運氣。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再點明哪個結果受影響及可做甚麼核查。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你與朋友要交雙人作品集，對方說寄出的檔案應已包括你最新頁面，但尚未開過合併檔。你想先一起核頁序及姓名，再寄給導師，不怪對方粗心。用一至兩句英文提議。

examples.en: I do not want to roll the dice on our submission when we can check the merged file together. Could we look at the page order and both names before sending it?
examples.zh: 明可一起核合併檔，我不想拿交件碰運氣；寄前可看看頁序及兩人名字嗎？

examples.en: Rather than roll the dice on whether my latest pages are included, let us open the final file once. We can confirm the order and credits together, then send it to the tutor.
examples.zh: 與其猜最新頁有否包括，不如開最後檔案一次；一起核次序與署名，再寄導師。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以共同核檔處理具體未知，保合作語氣，不把一項待核資料變成人身責備。

takeaways.en: They refused to roll the dice on the translation and asked the speaker to check the quotation before printing it.
takeaways.zh: 他們不願拿翻譯碰運氣，印前請說話者核引文。

takeaways.en: I was rolling the dice on finding my notes at the venue, so I checked the bag before leaving.
takeaways.zh: 我原本在碰運氣以為場地會找到筆記，所以出發前先核袋子。

lessons.titleZh: 全面禁止

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The council decided not to ban outright every outdoor activity.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page135, table1, row6; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Prohibit something completely rather than restrict it in limited circumstances.
brief.meaningZh: 完全禁止某事，而不是只限制某些情況。
brief.grammar: ban an activity outright is the usual object placement; ban outright + object is possible with emphasis. Banned/banning double n. Outright means completely here.
brief.register: Natural prohibition collocation; not a separate idiom and not necessarily a statement about law.
brief.boundaryZh: 禁某時段、音量或一個做法，不一定等於全面禁整活動；提議也不等於已定案。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需保留禁止對象、範圍及決定狀態，不能把調整誤說成全面禁。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分全面禁止與有範圍安排，提出符合實際決定的說法。

listening.en: The club did not ban outright every lunchtime performance; it asked groups to finish before the reading session began, so music remained possible in the earlier part of lunch.
listening.zh: 俱樂部沒有全面禁止每種午間演出；只請各組在閱讀開始前完結，所以午餐較早時仍可有音樂。
listening.promptZh: 規定的實際範圍是甚麼？

options.en: Performances could continue earlier, with a finishing time before reading began.
options.zh: 較早仍可演出，但閱讀開始前需完。

options.en: Every performance was prohibited at every time of the day.
options.zh: 每天所有時段都禁止所有演出。

options.en: The reading session was cancelled so that performances could continue without a limit.
options.zh: 取消閱讀，讓演出不限時繼續。

options.en: The club had only discussed an idea and had not asked groups to change anything.
options.zh: 俱樂部只談想法，尚未請各組改任何安排。

listening.explanationZh: did not ban outright及before限定非全面禁，仍有較早演出空間。

reply.promptEn: Why can the band still play during lunch?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼樂隊午餐時仍可演出？

options.en: The club chose not to ban outright every performance, but set a finishing time.
options.zh: 俱樂部沒全面禁每種演出，只設完結時間。

options.en: Music is still allowed before the reading session starts.
options.zh: 閱讀活動前仍准音樂。

options.en: The arrangement limits when we finish rather than removing all performances.
options.zh: 安排限制何時完，不是刪所有演出。

options.en: We can use the earlier part of lunch under the new timing rule.
options.zh: 新時段規則下，我們可用午餐較早部分。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都分時段限制與全面禁止，不把保留演出誤為完全沒規則。

scene.promptZh: 畫室禁止用噴霧顏料，但仍准水彩及鉛筆；有人說畫畫全禁了。哪句準確？

options.en: The studio has restricted one material, not banned drawing outright.
options.zh: 畫室限制一種物料，不是全面禁止畫畫。

options.en: Every drawing method is prohibited, including the watercolours it still allows.
options.zh: 每種畫法都禁，包括仍准的水彩。

options.en: No rule has changed because some materials remain allowed.
options.zh: 因仍准部分物料，所以沒有規則改。

scene.explanationZh: 一種物料受限不代全部活動被禁，也不是毫無改動。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種情況最不像 ban something outright？

options.en: 完全不准某項活動。
只改演出完結時間，仍保留較早時段。
取消全部參加某項活動的安排。

contrast.explanationZh: 保留較早時段是限制，不是全面禁止。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說：「閱讀前要完，就是叫我們不要再演吧？」你想澄清可保留的時段。哪句最好？

options.en: They have not banned us outright; we can still perform if we finish before the reading starts.
options.zh: 沒有全面禁我們；只要閱讀前完仍可演。

options.en: Yes, the earlier performance slot has been removed along with every other one.
options.zh: 是，較早演出時段也與所有其他時段一同刪掉。

options.en: There is no finishing time, so we can continue throughout the reading.
options.zh: 沒有完結時間，所以可整段閱讀繼續演。

dialogue.explanationZh: 回答仍可怎參與，同時保真正時間限制。

speaking.en: We chose not to ban outright every informal performance, but to agree when each one should finish.
speaking.zh: 我們沒選全面禁止每種非正式演出，而是議定各場何時完。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分全面禁止與具體限制的範圍。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：小組做訪問時，有人想因一次背景聲太大，往後全禁錄音。你想先改成安靜房間、開錄前問受訪者意願，並試短段聲音；用一至兩句英文提出有範圍的替代。

examples.en: We need not ban recording outright because one interview was noisy. Could we use a quiet room, ask the speaker first and test a short section before continuing?
examples.zh: 不用因一次訪問嘈吵就全面禁錄音；可用安靜房、先問說話者，再試短段才續嗎？

examples.en: Rather than ban outright every recorded interview, let us change the conditions that caused the problem. A quiet setting, the speaker’s agreement and a brief sound check would give us a better basis for deciding.
examples.zh: 與其全面禁每次錄音訪問，不如改造成問題的條件；安靜環境、說話者同意及短聲檢，會給較好決定基礎。

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出處理已知噪音的條件及本人同意，不用一次問題直接取代所有未來判斷。

takeaways.en: The school did not ban the sketches outright; it asked the writers to remove the personal remarks before submitting them again.
takeaways.zh: 學校沒全面禁短劇，只請作者刪人身評論再交。

takeaways.en: The club discussed whether to ban the equipment outright or allow a supervised trial before making its decision.
takeaways.zh: 俱樂部決定前，討論全面禁器材，還是准有指導試用。

lessons.titleZh: 過度保護、令對方無法嘗試

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Parents need not keep wrapping people in cotton wool.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page135, table1, row7; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Protect someone so much that ordinary experience or independent action is prevented.
brief.meaningZh: 保護過多，以致妨礙對方獲得一般經驗或獨立行動。
brief.grammar: wrap someone in cotton wool; wrapped/wrapping double p. Often criticism of excessive protection, not a rejection of all support.
brief.register: Informal idiom, especially familiar in British English.
brief.boundaryZh: 不表示所有協助都多餘，也不等於應撤去準備或當事人需要的支援。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要比較有用協助與替人做掉其願意嘗試的部分，不能只因有幫忙便叫過度保護。
brief.outcomeZh: 能感謝支援並協商可自己完成的範圍。

listening.en: My sister said I was wrapping her in cotton wool when I offered to answer every question at her first club visit; she wanted me nearby, but wanted to introduce herself and choose her own activity.
listening.zh: 妹妹說我提議在她首次到俱樂部代答所有問題，是過度保護；她想我在附近，但想自己介紹及選活動。
listening.promptZh: 妹妹希望怎樣改變幫忙方式？

options.en: Keep support nearby while letting her speak and choose for herself.
options.zh: 保留附近支援，但讓她自己說話及選擇。

options.en: Have every answer and activity chosen for her before arriving.
options.zh: 到達前替她選好每個答案與活動。

options.en: Remove all nearby support even though she had asked for it.
options.zh: 即使她要求，仍撤去所有附近支援。

options.en: Cancel the visit because she had decided she did not want any activity.
options.zh: 因她已決定不想參與任何活動，取消到訪。

listening.explanationZh: wanted nearby與introduce herself並存，要求不是全代做或全撤支援。

reply.promptEn: Why did your sister object to your offer to answer everything?
reply.promptZh: 妹妹為甚麼反對你代答所有問題的提議？

options.en: She felt I was wrapping her in cotton wool instead of letting her try.
options.zh: 她覺我在過度保護，不讓她試。

options.en: She wanted a chance to introduce herself with me still nearby.
options.zh: 她想我仍在附近，但有機會自己介紹。

options.en: My offer took over a part of the visit she wanted to manage.
options.zh: 我的提議接管了她想自己處理的到訪部分。

options.en: Being supported did not mean she wanted her choices made for her.
options.zh: 想有人支援不等於想讓人替她選擇。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都分支援與接管，沒有推成拒所有幫忙。

scene.promptZh: 導師讓新成員先排練一次，再自己向小組介紹作品，並留在旁邊答需要的問題。哪句最準確？

options.en: That is support for an independent attempt, rather than necessarily wrapping someone in cotton wool.
options.zh: 那是支援獨立嘗試，不一定是過度保護。

options.en: The member will repeat a script chosen entirely by the tutor, rather than prepare an introduction of her own.
options.zh: 成員會重讀全由導師選的稿，不是準備自己介紹。

options.en: The tutor has decided to give the whole introduction instead of the member.
options.zh: 導師已決定代成員做整個介紹。

scene.explanationZh: 有準備及在旁協助，仍讓本人嘗試，不因有支援便判過度保護。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「不要 wrap someone in cotton wool」推出？

options.en: 可讓人參與自己願試的普通活動。
應一併撤去對方要求的所有支援和準備。
可問當事人想自己處理哪部分。

contrast.explanationZh: 反過度保護不等於全撤所需協助。

dialogue.promptZh: 妹妹說：「你可陪我去，但不要替我自我介紹嗎？」你想尊重她的選擇。哪句最好？

options.en: Of course. I do not want to wrap you in cotton wool; I will stay nearby while you introduce yourself.
options.zh: 當然。我不想過度保護你；你介紹時我會在附近。

options.en: I could give the introduction first, and you could add something after I have introduced you.
options.zh: 我可先介紹你，你在我解釋完後再加一點。

options.en: I will write the answers you should read out, so you only need to say the words I choose.
options.zh: 我會寫你應讀的答案，你只需說我選的字句。

dialogue.explanationZh: 本人要求自己介紹；先代說或替選答案仍接管表達，而在旁支援可保本人選擇。

speaking.en: I can support you without wrapping you in cotton wool, so tell me which part you want to try yourself.
speaking.zh: 我可支援而不過度保護，所以請說想自己試哪部分。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再協商支援與獨立嘗試的範圍。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友原想參加試演，你因怕他落選難過，未問便替他取消報名。現在你發現這種保護拿走了他的選擇，想道歉、承認自己過度保護，問他是否希望你幫忙詢問能否恢復報名，不自行替他再報。用一至兩句英文向他道歉。

examples.en: I was wrapping you in cotton wool when I cancelled your audition entry because I feared you might be disappointed. I am sorry; would you like me to ask whether it can be restored, or would you rather handle that yourself?
examples.zh: 我因怕你失望而取消試演報名，是在過度保護你。對不起；你想我詢問能否恢復，還是想自己處理？

examples.en: Trying to spare you a possible rejection turned into wrapping you in cotton wool and taking away your choice. I should have asked, and I will not make another decision about the entry without you.
examples.zh: 想替你避開可能落選，變成過度保護、拿走你的選擇。我本應先問，不會再沒問你就決定報名的事。

writing.selfCheckZh: 承認過度保護已剝奪朋友選擇，為自己的行動道歉，讓對方決定下一步；不以好意免責，也不自行重新報名或假定可恢復。

takeaways.en: She did not want to wrap her brother in cotton wool, so she asked which part of the introduction he wished to handle himself.
takeaways.zh: 她不想過度保護弟弟，所以問介紹哪部分想自己處理。

takeaways.en: They worried about wrapping the children in cotton wool when they corrected every line before the children could share their own stories.
takeaways.zh: 孩子分享故事前，大人先改每行，他們擔心這是在過度保護。

lessons.titleZh: 自己將參與的是甚麼

target.pattern: \bwhat (?:I am|you are|he is|she is|we are|they are|I was|you were|he was|she was|we were|they were) getting into\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Climbers should know what they are getting into.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page135, table1, row9; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: The nature, demands or possible difficulties of an activity or commitment one is about to enter.
brief.meaningZh: 自己即將參與的活動或承諾的性質、要求或可能困難。
brief.grammar: know/understand/ask what someone is getting into; embedded clause has statement word order, not what are they getting into after know.
brief.register: Natural spoken embedded-question frame, often used before committing; different from get into music meaning develop interest.
brief.boundaryZh: 知道要求不等於保證沒有困難，也不是已接受所有條件；未知可先問。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需具體了解時間、角色或責任，不能只看吸引標題便說已知全部。
brief.outcomeZh: 能在答應之前問關鍵條件，保留選擇與誠實承諾。

listening.en: Before joining the weekend theatre project, I asked about rehearsals and the final performance so I knew what I was getting into; the poster sounded exciting, but it had not said whether we needed both weekends.
listening.zh: 加入周末劇場項目前，我問排練與最後演出，以了解將參與甚麼；海報吸引，但沒寫是否兩個周末都需到。
listening.promptZh: 說話者為甚麼再問？

options.en: The poster left a relevant time commitment unclear before the decision.
options.zh: 決定前，海報未交代一項相關時間承諾。

options.en: The speaker had already attended both weekends and was only reviewing the finished show.
options.zh: 說話者已參加兩周末，只在回顧完成演出。

options.en: The project had no rehearsals or performance and the speaker knew that from the poster.
options.zh: 項目沒排練或演出，說話者已從海報知道。

options.en: Asking about time meant the speaker had agreed to every possible extra session.
options.zh: 問時間表示已答應每個可能額外環節。

listening.explanationZh: before joining及海報未寫兩周，支持先了解再決定，不是問便已全答應。

reply.promptEn: Why did you ask about rehearsals before signing up?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼報名前問排練？

options.en: I wanted to know what I was getting into before committing both weekends.
options.zh: 承諾兩周末前，我想了解將參與甚麼。

options.en: The poster did not tell me how much time the project required.
options.zh: 海報沒寫項目需多少時間。

options.en: An exciting description was not enough to settle whether I could attend.
options.zh: 吸引的描述未足以決定我能否到。

options.en: I needed the rehearsal details to make an honest decision about joining.
options.zh: 我需排練細節，才能誠實決定參加。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答了解時間要求的目的，不假設一問便作承諾。

scene.promptZh: 朋友邀你代管班報一週，只說「很簡單」，卻還未交代要回稿、排版或印刷。你想先弄清角色。哪句最好？

options.en: I would like to know what I am getting into before I agree to cover the week.
options.zh: 答應代管一週前，我想知自己將參與甚麼。

options.en: Calling it simple confirms that I already know every responsibility.
options.zh: 說簡單便確認我已知每項責任。

options.en: I have finished the week’s editing, so I no longer need to learn the role.
options.zh: 我已完成一週編輯，不再需了解角色。

scene.explanationZh: 先問責任與尚未答應一致，不讓概括詞代實際工作。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解最不符合 know what someone is getting into？

options.en: 了解將參與事情的要求。
知道要求就保證永遠不會遇到困難。
可在承諾前問時間或角色。

contrast.explanationZh: 了解並不保證全程容易，也不是全接受額外要求。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「你問這麼多，是已決定不加入吧？」你其實等時間資料才可答。哪句最好？

options.en: Not necessarily. I want to understand what I am getting into so I can give you a realistic answer.
options.zh: 未必。我想了解將參與甚麼，好給你實際答案。

options.en: I only need to know the ticket price, rather than which weekends I would need to attend.
options.zh: 我只需知道票價，不是排練需哪些周末。

options.en: I would look at the same poster again instead of asking the organiser for the missing dates.
options.zh: 我會再看同一海報，不向主辦方問缺的日期。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需要的是缺少的時間要求；換問票價或重看沒日期的海報，不足以給實際參加答案。

speaking.en: I want to understand what I am getting into before I promise the time the project needs.
speaking.zh: 我想先了解將參與甚麼，才承諾項目所需時間。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再用陳述句次序組成what後的內嵌問句。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你已接下社區棋賽統籌，接之前知道要排每周賽程及聯絡參加者。首月遇到數次臨時退出，實際跟進比預期多。你想在檢討會說明，了解原有要求不等於遇不到難處，並請一起商量如何分擔已出現的聯絡工作。用一至兩句英文發言。

examples.en: I knew what I was getting into when I agreed to organise the weekly matches, but the late withdrawals have created more follow-up than I expected. Could we review how to share those calls rather than assume that understanding the role makes it easy?
examples.zh: 答應組織每周賽事時，我知道要承擔甚麼，但臨時退出令跟進比預期多。可否檢討怎分擔這些電話，而不假定了解職務就會輕鬆？

examples.en: Knowing what I was getting into helped me accept the schedule, but it did not remove the difficulty of rearranging matches after withdrawals. I would like us to agree who can help with the extra contact work now that we have seen it happen.
examples.zh: 了解自己要承擔甚麼，幫我接受了賽程，但沒有消除參加者退出後重排賽事的難處。既然已見到這情況，我想一起議定誰可幫額外聯絡。

writing.selfCheckZh: 區分已了解並接受的基本工作，與實際發生後才見到的跟進負擔；用已發生情況請求分工，不把了解要求等同完全沒有難度或自己沒承諾。

takeaways.en: She asked to see the rota so she could understand what she was getting into before offering to lead the group.
takeaways.zh: 她請看輪值表，好在自薦帶組前了解將承擔甚麼。

takeaways.en: We knew what we were getting into when we agreed to prepare two versions of the scene, though the work still challenged us.
takeaways.zh: 答應準備兩版場景時，我們知道將做甚麼，雖工作仍有挑戰。

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese personally compared against each English subject, polarity, qualification and referent; no human approval claimed.
